title: Stormwater, vegetation and runoff protection
moduleTitle: Group (Exterior, height & access): Workload and cost
audience: Trainee or new worker on the pressure cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify conditions, authorisation limits and evidence requirements relevant to stormwater, vegetation and runoff protection.
Differentiate worker-observable conditions from determinations reserved to qualified roof, electrical, chemical or environmental specialists.
Demonstrate a proportionate stop-work, referral and documented client communication using a paper-based scenario.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the pressure cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level pressure work and elevated or roof-level applications. High-pressure water, hoses and lances, electrical supply, exhaust gases and falls are all hazards on this track. Work above ground level is restricted to workers who are authorised by the employer and who hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Learning purpose and outcome
instruction.body: Explain why stormwater, vegetation and runoff protection changes the risk and permission profile of a roof-cleaning job. Learners must distinguish direct observation, tentative inference and specialist approval. No real roof work takes place in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Authorisation and boundary review
instruction.body: Using a simulated job pack, identify the site controller, stated job scope, contractor competencies, authorised exclusions, and missing permits relevant to stormwater, vegetation and runoff protection. A customer request alone never validates access or controls.

instruction.heading: Hazard recognition and hierarchy
instruction.body: Analyse this scenario: A downpipe drains toward a creek and planting beds; wash-water capture has not been planned. Begin with alternatives that avoid working at height. Mark fragile areas, skylights, public exposure, electrical installations and environmental unknowns wherever relevant; do not invent specialist approvals.

instruction.heading: Safe decision and escalation
instruction.body: The controlling principle is: Do not allow uncontrolled chemical wash water to enter stormwater, soil or waterways. Prepare a restricted-scope or stop-work decision. Identify which roof, electrical, work-at-height, chemical or environmental professional must resolve outstanding safety matters.

instruction.heading: Documentation and communication
instruction.body: Record what is known, the provenance of photographic or paper evidence, the person notified, the decision owner, and the unresolved approval. Never issue an unconditional safety or compliance certificate.

instruction.heading: Facilitated simulated practice
instruction.body: Conduct the paper-based exercise: Trace a fictional site drainage plan and document containment questions for an environmental specialist. The trainer examines reasoning, absence of unsupported assurances, escalation accuracy and readable records; no hazardous activity is simulated physically.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. In NSW, electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs an electrical licence or certificate. Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician, and plain panel washing is not stated by the official pages to need a licence. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Review the simulated job pack for the site controller, stated scope, contractor competencies, authorised exclusions and missing permits.
Treat a customer request alone as not validating access or controls.
Trace the drainage paths from the roof on the site plan, including any nearby waterway, soil or planting bed.
Identify fragile areas, skylights, public exposure, electrical installations and environmental unknowns.
Consider alternatives that avoid working at height before any roof method is chosen.
Keep uncontrolled chemical wash water out of stormwater, soil and waterways.
Where wash-water capture has not been planned, hold the job and put the containment questions in writing to an environmental specialist.
Record what is known, the source of the evidence, the person notified, the decision owner and the unresolved approval, and never issue an unconditional safety or compliance certificate.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. In NSW, electrical wiring work, including repairing, needs an electrical licence or certificate. Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician, and plain panel washing is not stated by the official pages to need a licence. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

qualityStandard: Drainage paths from the roof, and any nearby waterway, soil or planting bed, are traced on the plan before work.
Uncontrolled chemical wash water is kept out of stormwater, soil and waterways.
Containment questions are put to an environmental specialist in writing, and the job is held until they are answered.
No unconditional environmental clearance is given.
summary: Stormwater, vegetation and runoff are considered before any roof wash, because uncontrolled wash water must not reach stormwater, soil or waterways.
Where a downpipe drains toward a creek or planting beds and no capture has been planned, the job is held and the risk is referred.
This paper task asks the learner to follow an invented stormwater layout and draft containment queries for an environmental expert.

knowledgeChecks.question: For Stormwater, vegetation and runoff protection, identify two required verified facts, one stop-work trigger, and the professional who owns an unresolved clearance.
options: The customer's verbal request and the cleaner's confidence; a stop-work trigger of a slow day; the cleaner who owns the clearance, and the weather looking fine
The price agreed and the cleaner's insurance; the client's garden as a stop-work trigger; the job's sales representative owns the clearance
The weather forecast and the paint colour; any stop-work trigger; the team leader owns the clearance, and the crew's preferred working hours on site
The site controller and the stated job scope; uncontrolled wash water reaching stormwater, soil or waterways; the relevant specialist owns an unresolved clearance

knowledgeChecks.question: Can a customer's request alone validate access or controls, according to the lesson?
options: Yes, if the customer signs the job sheet
Yes, if the price has been agreed
No, a customer request alone never validates access or controls
